languages.name: English
languages.style: Source language. Short, plain, friendly sentences. Sentence case on the web, Title Case for buttons and titles on iOS and Android, as the apps already do.

languages.name: Indonesian
languages.style: Address the user with "Anda". Natural, friendly everyday Indonesian as in popular productivity apps, no stiff officialese.

languages.name: German
languages.style: Address the user with informal "du" (lowercase). Friendly and direct. Buttons use the infinitive ("Speichern", "Space löschen"). Avoid needless anglicisms, but keep established product terms from the glossary.

languages.name: Spanish
languages.style: Neutral international Spanish, address the user with "tú". Buttons use the infinitive ("Guardar", "Eliminar espacio").

languages.name: French
languages.style: Address the user with "vous". Buttons use the infinitive ("Enregistrer", "Supprimer l’espace"). Use French typography: a narrow no-break space before : ; ? ! and typographic apostrophes.

languages.name: Italian
languages.style: Address the user with informal "tu". Buttons use the infinitive ("Salva" is also fine where it is the established UI verb).

languages.name: Portuguese (Brazil)
languages.style: Brazilian Portuguese, address the user with "você". Friendly and simple.

languages.name: Turkish
languages.style: Address the user informally ("sen" forms), as most Turkish consumer apps do. Buttons use the short imperative ("Kaydet", "Sil").

languages.name: Russian
languages.style: Address the user with "вы" (lowercase). Buttons use the infinitive or short imperative common in Russian UIs ("Сохранить", "Удалить").

languages.name: Arabic
languages.style: Modern Standard Arabic. Right-to-left. Prefer neutral verbal nouns for buttons ("حفظ", "حذف"). Keep Western digits as the apps format numbers themselves.

languages.name: Hindi
languages.style: Address the user with "आप". Everyday Hindi as used in popular Indian apps: keep common English tech words that people actually say (ऐप, लिंक, ईमेल) instead of heavy Sanskritised terms.

languages.name: Japanese
languages.style: Polite です/ます style for sentences, short noun forms for buttons and titles ("保存", "スペースを削除"). No spaces between Japanese words.

languages.name: Korean
languages.style: Polite 해요체 for sentences, short noun forms for buttons and titles ("저장", "스페이스 삭제").

languages.name: Chinese (Simplified)
languages.style: Simplified Chinese for mainland China. Address the user with "你". Use full-width Chinese punctuation, no spaces between Chinese characters, a space between Chinese and Latin words is optional but be consistent.
